reality_delta: Planned hardening improves completeness gate precision and verification depth, but relies on regex word boundaries for Chinese text which typically fail with \b in non-Unicode-aware engines, and leaves verification receipt semantics undefined.
main_concern: Word-boundary gate matching for Chinese intent marker '处理这些风险点' may silently fail because standard \b boundaries do not recognize CJK characters as word characters, risking false negatives or bypasses.
top_risks: Chinese marker gate fails to match due to regex engine \b behavior with CJK characters.
Verification receipts lack defined schema or external attestation, potentially becoming self-check-only under another name.
Dispatcher permission tightening may inadvertently block legitimate cross-module calls or create escalation paths if deny-list semantics are misapplied.
missing_evidence: Regex engine documentation proving Unicode word boundary support for CJK.
Formal receipt schema with signer identity and non-repudiation mechanism.
Stop hook differential analysis showing no weakening of enforcement.
False positive/negative test matrix for gate matching before and after change.
minimum_fix: Replace \b-based boundaries for Chinese markers with explicit delimiters or Unicode-aware assertions; define receipt schema requiring execution metadata rather than command-name existence; preserve Stop hook deny/final-claim semantics exactly.

anti_loop_signal.reason: No iteration cap, recursion depth limit, or explicit loop-breaker introduced in described changes.
